contract: flop-devnet-lab shared rules, first recorded as the code behaved at 3ae1cdfa55707dd8e02678acdba57faec5aa50bf
status: A record of how the code behaves, not a specification of intent. It began at 3ae1cdf as a snapshot with no fixes in it. Since then fixes are recorded here too, with their vectors: an entry marked fixed says what changed and how it behaves now, and an entry marked current behavior is still a snapshot.

MIN_CAP.imd-flop: src/policy.ts MIN_CAP (its own literal; test/contract.test.ts checks it against this value)

FLOP_DECIMALS.note: money stage 1. Base units per FLOP are 10^18. Per FLOP's own sources, read 2026-11-11: the chain counts money in whole base units, 10^18 per FLOP, and its spec forbids floating point conversion in encoders. The viewer shows an exact amount as FLOP with this many decimals.

EXACT_AMOUNT_BOUND.note: money stage 1. 2^128, written as a digit string because a JSON number cannot hold it exactly. An exact amount is below it: per FLOP's own sources, read 2026-11-11, the chain holds money in a u128. The exact amount rule (amount.ts exactAmount, build-lane.py exact) is pinned by vectors/exact-amount.json.

UNRESOLVED.viewer: build-lane.py unresolved() (its own literal; viewer/test_contract_vectors.py checks it against this value)
UNRESOLVED.note: ledger states of a call whose outcome is not known. A row in one of them disagrees with any receipt until a read is booked for it.

DISAGREE.value: receipt and ledger disagree; reservation held, chain-final green blocked
DISAGREE.imd-flop: src/settlement.ts DISAGREE (run and receipt --refresh stderr when the booking step refuses a read, and receipt --refresh stderr when its append fails; the status of a receipt shown by run, receipt <id> and status when settlement.ts reconcile says disagree). A refresh that cannot take the ledger lock prints receipt-store.ts LEDGER_BUSY instead: a busy ledger is not a disagreement.

PAST_ADMITTED.value: booked past what the cap admitted; the day may end over its cap
PAST_ADMITTED.imd-flop: src/settlement.ts PAST_ADMITTED (run and receipt --refresh stderr, and the reason of the row, when a booking puts the day in a state the cap did not admit: a released hold that comes back, or a charge raised above the call's padded quote)

IDENTITY.value: receipt identity mismatch; chain-final green blocked

MAX_TOKENS_RANGE.note: per-part ranges differ today; see quirk Q-MAXTOK-RANGE

quirks.summary: imd-flop padQuote does not require estimated_output_tokens >= max_tokens or input tokens >= 1; spend-guard refuses such quotes.

imd-flop accepts a missing token count as 0, fractional counts and counts above 10M; spend-guard requires nonnegative integer counts <= MAX_TOKEN_COUNT. Both refuse a negative count: imd-flop padQuote returns null for it (swarm audit of 8ddc5d2, finding 11; before, a negative count shrank the divisor and inflated the pad).

imd-flop cap set / --per-call / --job-budget parse with JS Number(): 0x10, ' 1 ', '1e3' are accepted. spend-guard --cap uses a strict ASCII decimal regex; nan/inf spellings pass the syntax check and are refused later.
Viewer amount() accepts negative numbers; imd-flop knownAmount/usableCapCharge and spend-guard spend_amount require >= 0.
quirks.fixed_behavior: Viewer amount() returns unknown (None) for a negative number, as imd-flop knownAmount/usableCapCharge and spend-guard spend_amount do. A negative cap_charge, spent_before, quote, cap or settled amount shows blank and is never subtracted. spend-guard json_number still passes a negative number through.

quirks.summary: imd-flop run accepts 1..8192 via Number() (so 0x10, 1e3 and ' 8 ' pass); quote does not check. spend-guard takes argparse int, 0..10M, refusing out-of-range before the estimate.
imd-flop keeps only the 4 documented receipt states (else null); spend-guard passes the state through as given; viewer only asks whether the state is in SETTLES.

'Failed read' differs: imd-flop refresh = not (http === 200 and an object body); spend-guard receipts.py = code != 200; viewer = http not in (None, 200) or a non-empty error, or flag key_expired (since [fix: KD-1] a failed read with its own 'key expired' wording, not the 'receipt read failed' flag). http null + no error is fresh in the viewer only; http 200 + error text is failed in the viewer only. Booking step, review of the audit 8ddc5d2 fixes: that is about a live read. For a stored receipt file, imd-flop settlement.ts reconcile uses the viewer's test (flag key_expired, or http not in (null, 200), or a non-empty error), so the two parts decide 'not compared' for the same files (reconcile.json).

imd-flop matchReceipt compares job/seat with !== (null equals null) and also checks correlation_id; viewer identity_ok needs each of request_id/job/seat/did to be a non-empty string on both sides and ignores correlation_id. A numeric seat on the receipt makes imd-flop matchReceipt throw TypeError (it builds the link path from the seat); the viewer reports it as a seat difference. Review of the audit 8ddc5d2 fixes: status no longer hands such a file to matchReceipt. A stored receipt whose seat is neither a string nor absent is listed by name under unreadable_receipts and the other receipts are shown. matchReceipt itself and receipt <id> are unchanged. Booking step, review of the audit 8ddc5d2 fixes: the row comparison of matchReceipt is settlement.ts identityDiff, and match output is unchanged. Review of the booking step: reconcile no longer uses identityDiff. It compares a stored receipt only when its identity matches by the viewer's rule exactly (settlement.ts sameAttempt, as build-lane.py identity_ok), so the two parts give the same verdict for stored files whatever the identity fields hold. Pinned by the reconcile-not-compared-identity-* vectors in reconcile.json (job, seat and did null, empty, absent or a number on both sides), which replace reconcile-identity-null-job-on-both-sides.

imd-flop counted only holder paid rows against the seat's daily cap (spentToday). With payer requester the daily cap did not apply: the only limits were the per-call cap and the job budget the caller supplies per job id, while the FLOP still came out of the seat's own gateway key. The viewer checked every row against the daily cap using spent_before, which on a requester row was the job's spend, and never showed the job budget (finding 5). spend-guard has no payer.
quirks.fixed_behavior: The seat's daily cap bounds every call the seat's key pays for, whoever the call is for. Today the gateway has no third party payment, so the seat's key pays for every call, and every call counts. Requester is an attribution label plus a second, narrower limit, the job budget. Limits by payer, in checked order: holder: daily cap. requester: daily cap, then job budget. imd-flop: spentToday sums every row of the seat for that provider and UTC day, with no payer filter. noRoom refuses on the first limit with nothing left. checkBudget, after noRoom and the per-call cap, refuses on the first limit the padded quote does not fit. Ledger rows: spent_before is the seat's spend today before the call, for every payer. job_spent_before is the job's requester spend before the call, and null on a holder row. viewer: SPEND_LIMITS lists the same limits in the same order, each with its own running total field. Review of the audit 8ddc5d2 fixes: the daily cap applies to every row, whatever its payer. A row whose payer is neither holder nor requester is checked against the daily cap, its spent_before read as the seat's total, and carries the spend flag 'payer unknown'. A requester row with no job_spent_before key was written before this rule, when its spent_before was the job's spend: its job budget left is job_budget - spent_before - cap_charge, and its daily cap cannot be checked. A limit that applies to a row and cannot be worked out (an input is unknown, or that case) shows a blank figure and '<limit> not checked'. That wording is a spend flag, or one amber chip in the place of the green chain final chip, which such a row never gets. The row keeps 'matches'. spend-guard has no payer and keeps no running total: it checks one call against one cap, so nothing changed there. Not built: when FLOP ships proxies or escrow pools and a call is funded by another account, that account's limit will bound the call and it will not count against the seat's cap. Pinned by cap-payer.json (imd-flop) and, in viewer-labels.json (viewer), the label-requester vectors, the label-unknown-payer vectors and label-holder-unknown-spent-before-daily-cap-not-checked.

quirks.summary: Viewer mismatch and disagree rows append a second red 'unknown' chip when the ledger state is timeout_unknown or error.
quirks.fixed_behavior: One status chip per row: such a row shows only [grey sent, red unknown]; its identity-mismatch or disagree text and flags stay in the row.

quirks.summary: A fresh refresh that is unusable (no settling state, or wrong identity) writes spend null over a previously booked spend; cap_charge stays.
quirks.fixed_behavior: A read that is not a fresh, identity-matched settlement leaves the booked spend, cap_charge and state alone; only a trusted read moves the state, never from settled/released back to pending (settlement.ts nextBooking). Same root as IMD TS M1 (cli.ts:451). Booking step, review of the audit 8ddc5d2 fixes: nextBooking and refreshBooking are now the one decision settlement.ts decideBooking, with the same rule. One change: the reported cost a row records may raise its cap_charge on any refresh, not only on one that reads a trusted settlement (known defect KD-9).

quirks.summary: receipt --refresh fills seat/did/ss58/network from the ledger only when no receipt file exists; an existing file without them (716819c-era) is not migrated.
quirks.fixed_behavior: receipt --refresh seeds seat/did/ss58/network from the ledger row whenever the stored file lacks seat or did (stored values still win); IMD TS low #9.

quirks.summary: A failed read with a wrong identity renders red 'unknown', not 'mismatch' (failed-read branch runs before the identity check).
A row with no receipt file shows no reservation line.
quirks.fixed_behavior: A row with no receipt file shows its reservation line (cap_charge, else quote_padded).

quirks.summary: A pre-send error message with a 0x + 64 hex hash is stored as [hash] in the ledger reason but printed raw on stderr. The swarm audit of 8ddc5d2 reported this again as its finding 12 (info). It stays as it is. The ledger reason is rewritten so that the secret scan can store the refused_local row, which is what releases the reservation (src/run.ts). The message on stderr is not rewritten. Pinned by vector run-pre-send-hash-on-stderr.

rules.text: Precedence: unreadable, then unknown, then identity mismatch, then disagree.
A failed read never shows 'matches' and never releases the reservation.
An unknown row beside a settled ledger keeps the reservation line and keeps chain-final green blocked.
The link column stays grey 'not checked' and never turns green from ledger data alone.

viewer_label_rules.referenced_by: Vectors name these ids in label_rules. Every id must be referenced by at least one vector; both loaders reject an unknown id.

vector_status.default: A vector without a status pins current behavior: each part asserts `expect`.
vector_status.known_defect: A vector with status "known_defect" names a defect id from known_defects. `expect` is today's exact output and IS asserted, so the suite stays green and documents the defect. `target` holds the agreed label per affected part and is NOT asserted yet; the step that fixes the defect moves `target` into `expect` and drops the status.
vector_status.fixed: A vector with status "fixed" names the defect (known_defects id) that a step 3 [fix: ...] commit closed. That commit moved the old target into expect, which IS asserted, and dropped target. A c7 snapshot case lists closed defects in fixed.

known_defects.source: independent review of the audit 8ddc5d2 fixes, reproduced 2026-11-11
known_defects.where: src/run.ts booked its own receipt read against the row it wrote before the call (sent), not the latest row of the request; src/receipt-store.ts refreshReceipt read the previous row, decided and appended without holding one ledger lock across the three steps
known_defects.today: when two readers book the same request, a booked known settlement can be lowered or a settling state replaced, with no DISAGREE. Reproduced with a stub whose readReceipt, which run awaits, first runs receipt <id> --refresh with a read of settled 0.07: an own read of settled 0.05 books 0.05, an own read of released 0 books 0 and frees the charge, an own pending read puts the row back to estimated at the padded quote
known_defects.target: one decision for every receipt read, booked under the ledger lock against the latest row of the request, by run and by receipt --refresh alike; a read that would lower a booked settlement is refused and DISAGREE is reported
known_defects.status: fixed: booking step, review of the audit 8ddc5d2 fixes
known_defects.fixed_behavior: settlement.ts decideBooking(prev, read, costReported) is the one decision: only a trusted read changes state or spend; a reported cost may raise a charge and never lowers it, on a hold and on a settlement alike; a read below a booked known settlement disagrees and state and spend stay; otherwise a proven settlement replaces the spend and its charge replaces the hold; the state never moves from settled/released to a pending state; a charge that is not a known amount is never replaced by a guess. booking.ts bookRead(h, requestId, read, info) is the one booking step: under the ledger lock it reads the latest row of the request, decides, and appends one row when a recorded field changes. run and receipt --refresh both call it. run prints DISAGREE on stderr when its own read is refused, as refresh does, and still records its reported cost and the HTTP status of its read. If the lock cannot be taken or the append fails after the paid call, run exits 1 as before: the sent row stays the latest row and keeps the reservation, and the answer is in the response file. Review of the booking step: the reported cost survives that. bookRead resolves the reported cost in one place: the caller's (only run has one), else the one the row records, else usage.cost_flop in the stored response file (response-store.ts storedReportedCost), each through reportedCost. A missing, unreadable or costless response file gives no cost, never 0. A later refresh so charges at least the reported cost and records it in cost_reported. Two trusted reads book the same spend and charge in either order. Pinned by imd-flop/test/booking.test.ts (the interleavings) and imd-flop/test/decision-properties.test.ts (the properties). The first build covered receipt reads only; the rows run writes when the paid call itself fails followed in KD-8. Since then a refresh that cannot take the ledger lock prints 'ledger busy; the receipt read was stored and nothing was booked' on stderr, not DISAGREE, and still exits 0.

known_defects.source: found while building the booking step, reproduced 2026-11-11; closed on the owner's decision
known_defects.where: src/run.ts, the catch around provider.complete: the timeout_unknown, error and refused_local rows were appended from the row written before the call (sent), not through the booking step
known_defects.today: when the paid call fails while another process refreshes the same request and books a settlement, run's failure row replaces it. Reproduced with a stub whose complete() first runs receipt <id> --refresh with a read of settled 0.3 (above the 0.186 hold), then fails: a timeout or an HTTP 500 leaves the latest row at timeout_unknown or error, spend null, cap_charge 0.186; a pre send failure leaves refused_local, cap_charge 0
known_defects.target: every ledger row run writes after the paid call goes through the booking step against the latest row of the request, under the ledger lock; a failure report never replaces a booked settlement
known_defects.status: fixed: booking step, review of the audit 8ddc5d2 fixes
known_defects.fixed_behavior: settlement.ts decideFailure(prev, failure) is the one decision for a failure report (timeout_unknown, error, or refused_local for a failure before anything was sent): a row in a settling state stays; a timeout or a gateway error moves a row that does not settle to timeout_unknown or error, and spend and charge stay; 'nothing was sent' releases the reservation (refused_local, cap_charge 0) only from a row still in state sent (review of the booking step: it released any row that does not settle, including reserved and estimated rows that only a trusted gateway read produces); a charge that is not a known amount is never replaced. booking.ts bookFailure(h, requestId, failure, info) books it under the ledger lock on the same step as bookRead. A booked report records run's reason and HTTP status on the row it moves. Review of the booking step: a report that is not booked is still recorded (it appended nothing before): one row keeps state, spend and charge exactly, with reason settlement.ts keptReason (the report named, 'booked settlement kept' or 'booked row kept') and the report's http. run keeps its exit code; its message says what the ledger kept, and when the ledger holds a settlement for the request it says so and does not call the spend unknown. Pinned by imd-flop/test/booking.test.ts and the decideFailure properties in imd-flop/test/decision-properties.test.ts. Review of the booking step closed the gap this left open: a trusted read that moves a refused_local row now holds the row's quote_padded again (raised by a reported cost), and when quote_padded is not a known amount the read disagrees and nothing changes (settlement.ts decideBooking). A trusted read and a 'nothing was sent' report book the same spend and charge in either order (decision-properties.test.ts).
